questions.q: What is the article's main argument?
options: California's wealth tax failed, but other states backed taxing the rich, mostly via income
Wealth taxes proved easier to pass than income taxes in the 2026 midterms
Billionaires' spending defeated nearly every tax-the-rich measure across the states
Voters rejected tax hikes on the rich everywhere, including income and second homes
questions.explain: The author says taxing income is proving more successful than taxing wealth.

questions.q: How much did Sergey Brin and other billionaires spend against Proposition 40?
questions.explain: They spent nearly $400 million to defeat it.

questions.q: What is Washington state's new tax rate on household income above $1 million?
questions.explain: Voters preserved a 9.9% income tax on household income above $1 million.

questions.q: What is Boulder, Colorado's new tax aimed at?
options: Short-term rentals booked through online platforms
Homes that sit empty more than half the year
Single-family homes valued at $5 million or more
Luxury condos and co-ops valued above $1 million
questions.explain: Voters approved a vacancy tax of roughly $4,000 a year, effective in 2028.

questions.q: Why does the author think income taxes are easier than wealth taxes?
options: Income is already reported on annual filings, while wealth needs valuations
Wealthy people hold most of their assets in cash that is easy to tax
Courts in most states have already banned wealth taxes outright
Federal law bars states from valuing assets held by billionaires
questions.explain: Income tax relies on annual filings; wealth taxes require valuing businesses, farmland and art.
